pm-master.title: The master checklist
pm-master.storageNote: Progress saves in this browser as you check items.

items.t: Walk the center: storefronts, sidewalks, parking field, lighting
items.n: Look for trip hazards, burned-out poles, cart damage, standing water.

items.t: Check the main field and remote lots for litter, illegal dumping, and cart corrals
items.n: Remote lots get skipped first; make them an explicit stop.

items.t: Inspect dumpster and rear service areas; confirm gates and enclosure
items.n: Rear-of-house condition shows up in tenant satisfaction first.

items.t: Review tenant communication queue; respond within one business day
items.n: Under the Operator Landlord approach, responsiveness is the product.

items.t: Confirm signage is lit and pylon faces are intact
items.n: Signage is common-area work that directly feeds leasing.

items.t: Run the rent cycle: statements, reminders, escalate delinquencies per the lease
items.n: Courtesy reminder before the first; defined escalation after.

items.t: Reconcile the rent roll to the bank; investigate every variance
items.n: A rent roll that does not match the bank is fiction.

items.t: Review the P&L against budget; annotate significant variances
items.n: An unexplained variance grows. A named explanation can be managed.

items.t: Issue owner report: income, expenses, occupancy, work, decisions needed
items.n: Same format every month — the report is a rhythm, not an event.

items.t: Check certificate of insurance expirations — tenants and vendors
items.n: Request renewals 30 days before lapse, in writing.

items.t: Review aged work orders; nothing open past 30 days without a reason
items.n: Every open order needs an owner and a next step.

items.t: Pull and re-file current COIs for every tenant and active vendor
items.n: Match against the lease-required coverages, not just presence.

items.t: Fire & life-safety inspection: extinguishers, exits, alarms, panels
items.n: Document with dated photos; file in the owner safe.

items.t: Meet or call each key vendor: roof, HVAC, landscaping, paving, security
items.n: Ask what they are seeing that you are not.

items.t: Review the critical-dates board: expirations, options, notice windows
items.n: Anything inside 12 months gets a named next step.

items.t: Walk the roof (or schedule the walk) and inspect fascia, gutters, drains
items.n: Roof problems are cheap at quarterly cadence and expensive at annual.

items.t: Test site lighting photometrics at night; replace dark poles
items.n: Lighting drives both safety perception and evening sales.

items.t: Spring: full exterior refresh — landscaping, pressure washing, striping touch-up
items.n: Curb appeal is leasing inventory.

items.t: Pre-summer (Gulf South by June 1): storm prep — trees trimmed, drains cleared, loose items secured
items.n: Document pre-storm condition with dated photos.

items.t: Summer: HVAC service verified on every suite; confirm contract coverage
items.n: Summer HVAC failure is a tenant-relations event, not a maintenance item.

items.t: Fall: parking lot inspection — cracks sealed before freeze or wet season
items.n: Water enters cracks; what freezes or floods lifts asphalt.

items.t: Winter: holiday operations plan — parking, signage, extended hours lighting
items.n: Set it in October, not November.

items.t: Build the operating budget for next year; set the reserve contribution
items.n: Fund the roofs and lots you already know you own.

items.t: Complete CAM reconciliation against actuals per the lease deadlines
items.n: Deadlines are lease obligations — verify your own language.

items.t: Full property condition survey: roof, envelope, paving, site, signage
items.n: Feed findings into the capital plan and the reserve study.

items.t: Insurance renewal review: values, coverages, claims history, bids
items.n: Start 120 days before expiry; never renew on autopilot.

items.t: Property tax assessment review; file appeals where warranted
items.n: Deadlines are jurisdictional — calendar them at the start of the year.

items.t: Update the emergency and continuity plan; confirm contact tree
items.n: Include tenants, vendors, insurer, counsel, and utilities.

items.t: A one-to-two-page abstract for every tenant, verified against the executed lease
items.n: Dates, rent schedule, options, exclusives, CAM treatment, notices.

items.t: Every executed lease, amendment, and side letter filed and named consistently
items.n: Suite_Tenant_DocumentType_Date.

items.t: Security deposit and guaranty on record for every suite
items.n: Note the gaps; missing deposits surface at the worst times.

items.t: Renewal alert set at 12 / 9 / 6 months before every expiration
items.n: Late renewal conversations are negotiated from weakness.

items.t: A vendor table: scope, contract terms, rates, COI expiration, contacts
items.n: One table, one home, current to the month.

items.t: Every service contract reviewed before auto-renewal
items.n: Diarize renewal windows the day the contract is signed.

items.t: Warranties on capital work filed in the owner safe with expiration dates
items.n: A warranty you cannot find is a warranty you do not have.

items.t: One source of truth for leases, vendors, work orders, and financials
items.n: If it is not in the system, it did not happen.

items.t: Backup verified: exports run, restore tested, off-site copy current
items.n: A backup that has never been restored is a hope.

items.t: Access review: who can reach the records, banking, and accounts — and should they
items.n: Quarterly, and after any staffing change.

items.t: The checklist itself reviewed and revised
items.n: Add what was missed; remove what no longer serves the property.

doc-safe.title: The owner document safe
doc-safe.storageNote: Progress saves in this browser as you check items.

items.t: Formation documents and operating agreement for every owning entity
items.n: Including amendments — the version history matters.

items.t: EIN records and registered agent documentation
items.n: Required for banking, tax filings, and counsel.

items.t: Recorded warranty deeds and the complete chain of title instruments
items.n: The paper that proves the asset is yours.

items.t: Title insurance policy and closing documents from acquisition
items.n: The title policy is the first call when a boundary or servitude question arises.

items.t: Corporate resolutions or authorizations naming who may act for the entity
items.n: Banks and title companies will ask for these.

items.t: The recorded plat and all recorded revisions
items.n: For a legacy center, the plat is the operating map — parking, easements, setbacks.

items.t: Surveys: original, ALTA/NSPS, and any as-builts
items.n: Marked-up survey copies belong here too.

items.t: Zoning records: classification, variances, and conditions of approval
items.n: Legacy variances (parking, green area) are assets — keep the paper that proves them.

items.t: Environmental reports: Phase I, Phase II, and any remediation records
items.n: Lenders and buyers will request these in every transaction.

items.t: Easements and servitudes: reciprocal access, utility, signage
items.n: Include recorded exhibits and a simple indexed list.

items.t: Every executed lease, amendment, side letter, and exhibit — complete and ordered
items.n: Sequence matters: a missing amendment changes what the lease says.

items.t: A verified lease abstract for every suite
items.n: One to two pages; verified against the executed documents.

items.t: Estoppel certificates collected from tenants at acquisition and refinance
items.n: Filed by suite, with the date of the certifying statement.

items.t: Guaranties and personal undertakings
items.n: Note which are active and which have been released.

items.t: Insurance obligations per lease: required coverages and minimum limits
items.n: So COIs can be checked against something written.

items.t: All property policies, renewals, and endorsements — current and historical
items.n: Historical policies matter for claims with long tails.

items.t: Claims file: FNOL, adjuster correspondence, settlements, and reserves
items.n: Close every claim to a final paper trail.

items.t: Tenant and vendor COIs, current year plus recent history
items.n: The active expirations also live in the operating system.

items.t: Flood and wind documentation where applicable — maps, elevation certificates, policies
items.n: In Gulf South markets, this family is first-class, not an afterthought.

items.t: Loan documents: note, mortgage, guarantees, and every amendment or modification
items.n: Include lender-required reporting commitments.

items.t: Appraisals and inspection reports from acquisition and refinance
items.n: They benchmark value in future conversations.

items.t: Tax assessments, bills, and appeal records by year
items.n: Win an appeal once and the record pays for itself annually.

items.t: Year-end financial statements and depreciation schedules
items.n: Hand your accountant a complete year, not an archaeology project.

items.t: Major service contracts: roof, HVAC, paving, landscaping, security
items.n: Diarized with expiration and renewal windows.

items.t: Capital work records: contracts, warranties, permits, and completion documents
items.n: Warranty + proof of install = enforceable protection.

items.t: Utilities: account numbers, meter locations, and service contracts
items.n: Someone other than you should be able to transfer service in an emergency.

items.t: The one-page access map: where the safe is, how it is organized, who holds keys and passwords
items.n: Sealed with counsel or a partner — the safe must survive its owner.

items.t: Redundancy verified: three copies, two media, one off-site — tested this year
items.n: A copy that has never been opened is a rumor.
